subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Braced Frames: Diagonals Save Buildings
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Braced Frames: Diagonals Save Buildings.

hook.text: Take the bracing out of a bookshelf and push sideways. It collapses instantly.

buildup.text: Diagonal bracing in buildings works identically. It turns rectangular frames into triangles that resist lateral forces.

discovery.text: X-bracing uses two diagonals crossing. One is in tension while the other handles compression.

twist.text: The John Hancock Center in Chicago shows its bracing on the outside. It cut steel usage by 40% and became iconic.

climax.text: Eccentric bracing intentionally creates a weak link that absorbs earthquake energy before the frame yields.

quiz.question: How did external bracing benefit the John Hancock Center?
options: It allowed more windows for natural lighting on every floor
It reduced steel usage by 40% while providing lateral stability
It eliminated the need for an internal elevator shaft
